newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CITY BIRD ORDERS 767S , MD-11 FREIGHTERS.
newsitem.headline: CITY BIRD ORDERS 767S , MD-11 FREIGHTERS.

text.p: Belgian low-fare, long-haul airline City Bird said on Thursday it would expand its fleet with two Boeing 767 planes and two McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighters in the next two years.
"The 767s are scheduled for next year, one in February and the other in April," City Bird president Victor Hasson said.

He told Reuters the two 268-seat planes would be on medium-term lease from Ansett Worldwide Aviation Services. One would be delivered directly by Boeing, the other had previously been leased to Vietnam Airlines.
The MD-11s were due to be delivered in early 1999, he said.
Asked about future expansion plans for City Bird, Hasson said: "We have done our programming for the next two years. In a few months we'll see about the next few years."
City Bird, 62.5-percent owned by Belgian group City Hotels, was launched in March.
It currently operates two MD-11 planes, mainly for services from Belgium to the U.S.
Swisscargo, Swissair's air-freight subsidiary, has bought the freight capacity on current MD-11 flights.
Asked whether Swisscargo might also be interested in taking the cargo capacity on the new MD-11 freighters, Hasson said: "At this stage, we have not decided (what to do with the capacity)".
